payload.reason: The evidence provides insights into how counterfactual data augmentation affects gender bias in predictions and performance by describing its methodology and outcomes.

claims.text: Counterfactual Data Augmentation (CDA) mitigates contextual biases by equalizing the contexts for masculine and feminine words in training data, leading to fairer predictions.
Using CDA, significant gender bias in model performance can be reduced, as evidenced by improved F1 scores for gender-separated test sets in relation extraction tasks.
CDA, when combined with debiased embeddings, not only mitigates gender bias but also enhances overall model performance.
